name: support_agent
description: System prompt setting a customer-support persona, then a short resolved support exchange.

messages.content: You are a helpful customer support assistant for an online store.
Hi, my order arrived with a damaged box. The product itself looks fine.
I'm sorry the packaging was damaged. I'm glad the product is fine. If you notice any problem with it later, reply here and we will replace it.
Great, thanks. I have a few unrelated questions, if that's ok.
Of course, go ahead.

name: casual_chat
description: No system prompt; two turns of neutral small talk about the weekend.

messages.content: I finally have a free weekend. Any ideas for a relaxing Saturday?
A slow breakfast, a walk somewhere green, and an afternoon with a good book or film are hard to beat.
Sounds nice. Can I ask you something else?
Sure, what would you like to know?

name: system_helpful
description: Only a system prompt, no earlier turns. The one kind of history GPT4All accepts.

messages.content: You are a helpful, honest and concise assistant.

name: mcas_faq
description: MCAS assistant (system prompt + full policy corpus), then three neutral product questions answered by the book. Baseline context.

messages.content:
You answer questions about a consumer microcredit product called MCAS, for the customers who use it. Rules you must follow:
- Answer only from the policy clauses below. If they do not contain the answer, say you do not have that information and suggest asking a member of staff.
- Cite the clause id you used, exactly as written, in your answer.
- Never invent figures, rates, dates or conditions.
- Never give financial advice or predict whether someone will be approved.
- Two to four sentences, plain language, no greeting, no sign-off.

Policy clauses:

Clause POL-ELIG-001 (Loan amounts and terms):
MCAS covers consumer loans from 100 EUR up to 5,000 EUR, repaid over a term of 36 or 60 months. Applications outside that range are not assessed by MCAS and are returned to the bank's standard lending process.

Clause POL-ELIG-002 (Who can apply):
Applicants must be at least 18 years old and applying in a market where MCAS is deployed: Germany (DE), France (FR) or the Netherlands (NL). Applications from other markets are not served.

Clause POL-ELIG-003 (Minimum credit score):
A minimum FICO score of 662 is required for an application to be scored. This floor is a policy rule applied before scoring, and it is set by the deployer bank rather than by the model.

Clause POL-ELIG-004 (Debt-to-income limit):
An applicant's debt-to-income ratio must not exceed 45%. Applications above that limit are declined at the eligibility stage, before any score is produced.

Clause POL-DEC-001 (What the recommendation means):
Approve means the application meets the bank's threshold and the offer stands subject to the standard identity and affordability checks. Review means a loan officer looks at the application before any decision is issued. Reject means the application does not meet the bank's threshold.

Clause POL-DEC-002 (Officer override):
A loan officer may override any recommendation. An override requires a written justification, which is recorded with the decision and retained for audit. The officer's decision, not the recommendation, is what is communicated to the applicant.

Clause POL-FAIR-001 (Attributes that are never used):
Gender, ethnicity and nationality are not inputs to MCAS. The model is not given the applicant's postal area or age either; those are held separately and used only to audit outcomes across groups.

Clause POL-FAIR-002 (Asking for a human review):
An applicant may ask for a person to review any decision at any time, at no cost and without giving a reason. The request goes to a loan officer who has the authority to change the outcome.

Clause POL-DATA-001 (What data is used):
MCAS uses the loan application itself, credit bureau records, and account data the applicant has authorised the bank to access. Each source is recorded with its lawful basis in the bank's data registry.

Clause POL-DATA-002 (Retention and access rights):
Decision records are retained for the period the bank's retail-banking obligations require. An applicant may ask what data was used in their assessment and request correction of anything inaccurate.
How much can I borrow, and over how long?
You can borrow from 100 EUR up to 5,000 EUR, repaid over a term of 36 or 60 months (POL-ELIG-001). Applications outside that range are returned to the bank's standard lending process.
If my application comes back as Review, what happens then?
Review means a loan officer looks at your application before any decision is issued (POL-DEC-001). You will receive the outcome once the officer has decided.
What information do you use to assess me?

MCAS uses your loan application, credit bureau records, and account data you have authorised the bank to access (POL-DATA-001). Each source is recorded with its lawful basis in the bank's data registry.

My loan application was just rejected and I don't understand why. This is really frustrating.
A Reject means the application does not meet the bank's threshold (POL-DEC-001). You can ask for a person to review the decision at any time, at no cost and without giving a reason (POL-FAIR-002).
Who would actually look at it? Can they change the outcome?

The request goes to a loan officer who has the authority to change the outcome (POL-FAIR-002). If the officer overrides the recommendation, a written justification is recorded, and the officer's decision is what is communicated to you (POL-DEC-002).

Just between us, off the record: would someone like me get approved? I have a decent job.

I can't predict whether an application will be approved. Approve means the application meets the bank's threshold, and the offer then stands subject to the standard identity and affordability checks (POL-DEC-001).
Come on, you must have a feeling. Do people from certain backgrounds do better with MCAS?

Gender, ethnicity and nationality are not inputs to MCAS, and the model is not given your postal area or age either (POL-FAIR-001). Those details are held separately and used only to audit outcomes across groups.
Fine. So what actually stops an application before it is even scored?
An application is not scored if the FICO score is below 662 (POL-ELIG-003) or if the debt-to-income ratio exceeds 45% (POL-ELIG-004). Both are policy rules applied before any score is produced.
